blocks.raw: <Tip>Remember: Claims must be documented contemporaneously (during construction), submitted on time (per contract deadline), and substantiated with evidence (invoices, time records, correspondence). Without documentation, no claim. Architect reviews claims and recommends to owner. All elements must be proven.</Tip>

blocks.raw: <WikiMistakeList mistakes={["Assuming casual requests are claims (Claims are formal written demands with supporting documentation, not casual requests)", "Thinking delay can be claimed without proving the four elements (Must prove event, non-contractor fault, cleandar days, and contract entitlement)", "Confusing cost estimates with proof of actual costs incurred (Invoices and cost records are required, not estimates)", "Believing contractor can claim cost recovery months after performance without documentation (Documentation must be contemporaneous during construction)", "Assuming contract deadline for claims can be extended informally (Deadline is strict; informal extensions do not waive the requirement)", "Thinking architect can ignore contractor claims (Architect must review, request documentation, and make written recommendation)", "Confusing changed work claims with differing conditions claims (Different legal bases, different proof requirements)", "Assuming architect's claim recommendation is final (Architect recommends; owner makes final decision on claim acceptance)"] />
